technologies.name: Parchment
technologies.description: Unlocks parchment and allows you to create written material.
technologies.flavor: Parchment became an important carrier of information in the ancient world.

technologies.name: Mathematics
technologies.description: -10% to the work cost of construction.
technologies.flavor: Ancient civilizations could count, but only now has knowledge moved from simple recipes to strict proofs. Geometry and abstract calculation let people not just watch the world but compute it: from the shape of a wheel's teeth to the motion of the stars.

technologies.name: Calendar
technologies.flavor: People have tracked the turning of the seasons since the earliest times, but only now has the calendar become a standard tool of management: precise planning of sowing, pruning and harvest let plantations reach their full potential.

technologies.name: Draft Animals
technologies.description: Unlocks the use of draft animals to turn millstones.
technologies.flavor: Draft animals let people harness animal strength for heavy work, greatly raising output and efficiency in farming and construction.

technologies.name: Water Wheel
technologies.description:
Unlocks the water mill: the running water sets the millstones in motion.
+25% to the production of mines, quarries, the bloomery, the smelter and the forge, where the water runs: the ore is washed and the bellows are driven by the water.
technologies.flavor: The water wheel became an important source of power in the ancient world, automating the processing of grain and other materials.

technologies.name: Cog Wheel
technologies.description:
Unlocks the toothed wheel: the gears that pass a rotation on to the working tool.
+25% to the production of mines, quarries, animal mills, oilmaker's houses, weaver's and silkmaker's houses, and of the mason's, carpenter's and jeweler's workshops.
technologies.flavor: A wheel that rolls is not yet a machine; the teeth are. They turn one turn of the axle into a turn of the millstone, a pull of the press or a lift of the winch, and they hold the load instead of letting it fall back. Vitruvius described a mill whose upright wheel drove a horizontal one through a row of teeth, and a marble saw driven the same way is known from a sarcophagus in Hierapolis.

technologies.name: Screw Press
technologies.description: Adds one production slot to the winemaker's house, the oilmaker's house, the dairy, the paper workshop and the jeweler's house.
technologies.flavor: A threaded spindle turns many easy turns of a long handle into one slow, enormous squeeze. The press no longer waits on the weight of a beam, and a second batch can be worked beside the first.

technologies.name: Hoisting Mechanisms
technologies.description: +10% to the production of mines and quarries.
technologies.flavor: A shaft is only as deep as the rope that serves it. A drum on a windlass, a rope over a pulley, a capstan walked round by men or oxen — and in the Chinese mines a treadwheel the size of a house, turning all day like the water wheel it resembles. What the hoist brings up is what the mine is worth: the ore that cannot be lifted stays in the rock.

technologies.name: Mechanics
technologies.description:
Adds one production slot to the animal mill and the water mill.
+10% to the production of the woodcutter's camp.
technologies.flavor: The workshops knew the lever and the pulley long before anyone wrote them down. Heron of Alexandria set the pieces in order in his Mechanics, and later al-Khazini weighed the same pieces of rope and iron in the Book of the Balance of Wisdom. A machine, they wrote, is what moves a load we could not lift: a wheel on an axle, a crank, a connecting rod, a frame to hold it all. From this the hoist, the press and the mill stop being clever tricks and become craft — they can be built again, and then improved.

technologies.name: Paper
technologies.description:
Allows you to build the paper workshop.
Allows you to produce paper from mulberry, hemp and ramie with the help of lime.
technologies.flavor: This revolutionary invention made it possible to create an affordable, practical material for writing.

technologies.name: Scriptoriums
technologies.flavor: In scriptoriums scribes copied, translated, rewrote and recensioned texts on administration, the worship of the gods, magic and the curing of disease.

technologies.name: Cartography
technologies.description: Allows scouts to explore areas in the fog of war.
technologies.flavor: The art of exploring the land and drawing maps of it.

unlock_effects.name: Allows scouts to explore areas in the fog of war.

technologies.name: Emporia
technologies.description: Allows you to build improvements on explored resource hexes outside the Region. Such an outpost needs a road to the city and costs coins on top of labour; the further from the city, the more expensive.
technologies.flavor: An emporion was neither a colony nor a city: a foothold on a foreign shore where the road met the sea and goods changed hands.

unlock_effects.name: Allows you to build improvements on explored resource hexes outside the Region.

technologies.name: Alchemy
technologies.description: Allows you to build the alchemist's house.
technologies.flavor: A protoscience of attempts to turn base metals into gold.

technologies.name: Steel Making
technologies.description: Unlocks steel in the forge and the goods forged of it.
technologies.flavor: Iron with a little carbon is another metal. Charcoal driven into a hot bloom and a flux that keeps the melt clean give a smith an edge that holds and a blade that does not bend.

technologies.name: Glassblowing
technologies.flavor: The first step towards the modern glass industry.

technologies.name: Hopping
technologies.description: Unlocks the recipe for hopped beer.
technologies.flavor: Hops made beer keep. Grain alone gave a drink that soured within days; a bittering charge of hops held it back, and beer became a good that could be stored and shipped.
